meta.title: The Story of the Lost Sheep
meta.verseText: "May your kingdom come. May what you want to happen be done on earth as it is done in heaven." • Matthew 6:10 NIrV
meta.theme: God's Kingdom — Jesus searches for the lost and makes a way for everyone to come home.

questions.text: What kind of animal wandered off in Jesus' story?
questions.hint: It says 'baa'!
questions.explanation: Jesus told the parable of the lost sheep. One sheep wandered away from the flock.

questions.text: How many sheep did the shepherd have in total?
questions.hint: It's a big round number.
questions.explanation: The shepherd had one hundred sheep, and one of them wandered off.

questions.text: How many sheep got lost in the story?
questions.hint: Just a single one.
questions.explanation: Only one sheep wandered off. The other ninety-nine stayed together.

questions.text: A short story Jesus used to teach something big about God is called a parable.
questions.hint: Jesus loved telling these.
questions.explanation: True! A parable is a short story that uses everyday things like seeds, coins, or sheep to teach a big truth about God.

questions.text: In which book of the Bible do we find the story of the Lost Sheep?
questions.hint: It starts with the letter L.
questions.explanation: The parable of the Lost Sheep is found in Luke 15:1-7.

questions.text: When the shepherd found his lost sheep, he felt ______.
questions.hint: It's a happy feeling.
questions.explanation: The shepherd wasn't angry or annoyed — he was joyful and wanted everyone to celebrate with him!

questions.text: What did the shepherd do when one sheep wandered off?
options: Stayed with the 99 and forgot it
Went out searching until he found it
questions.hint: He didn't give up.
questions.explanation: The shepherd cared so much that he went out searching until he found the one lost sheep.

questions.text: Some religious leaders grumbled because Jesus spent time with all kinds of people, even those who made bad choices.
questions.hint: They were grumpy about His friends.
questions.explanation: True! The religious leaders grumbled, 'Why is Jesus spending time with those kinds of people?' But Jesus wanted everyone to know how much God cares.

questions.text: What did the shepherd say after he found his sheep?
options: "Come celebrate with me! I found my sheep!"
questions.hint: He invited others to be happy with him.
questions.explanation: The shepherd was so excited he told everyone, 'Come celebrate with me! I found my sheep!'

questions.text: According to Jesus, who gets really happy when even ONE person turns back to God?
questions.hint: It's a place up high.
questions.explanation: Jesus said that when even one person turns back to God, all of heaven gets really happy!

questions.text: In the story, every single person is like the ______ sheep.
questions.hint: It wandered away.
questions.explanation: Jesus told this story because every single person is like that lost sheep — we all wander away from God.

questions.text: What takes us farther away from God, like the sheep wandering off?
questions.hint: It's the wrong things we choose to do.
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches that sin takes us farther away from God, just like the sheep wandered away from the shepherd.

questions.text: How did Jesus take care of the problem of our sin?
options: By dying on the cross to pay for our sins
questions.hint: He gave His life for us.
questions.explanation: Jesus took care of our sin by dying on the cross to pay for it, because we matter so much to Him.

questions.text: What is this week's Bottom Line?
options: Jesus made a way for you to be part of God's kingdom
questions.hint: It's about belonging to God's kingdom.
questions.explanation: The Bottom Line is: Jesus made a way for you to be part of God's kingdom.

questions.text: This month, the kids are learning about God's ______ and the treasures of knowing Jesus.
questions.hint: A king rules over this.
questions.explanation: This month's theme is God's Kingdom and the treasures that come with a life of knowing Jesus.

questions.text: Sheep are very good at paying attention and never wander off.
questions.hint: Think about how sheep act in the story.
questions.explanation: False! Sheep aren't very good at paying attention — they just munch and wander until they get stuck or walk in circles.

questions.text: Just like the shepherd carried the sheep, who carries us back to God?
questions.hint: He made a way for us.
questions.explanation: Just like the shepherd carried the sheep, Jesus carries us back to God.

questions.text: What is this month's Memory Verse reference?
questions.hint: It's part of the Lord's Prayer.
questions.explanation: The Monthly Memory Verse is Matthew 6:10 (NIrV).

questions.text: Fill in the memory verse: "May your ______ come. May what you want to happen be done on earth as it is done in heaven."
questions.hint: It matches this month's theme.
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:10 says, 'May your kingdom come. May what you want to happen be done on earth as it is done in heaven.'

questions.text: Why did Jesus spend time with people who made bad choices?
options: He wanted everyone to understand how much God cares
questions.hint: It's about God's love for everyone.
questions.explanation: Jesus wasn't bothered by the grumbling; He wanted everyone to understand how much God cares.

questions.text: Why does the story teach that even ONE lost person matters so much to God?
options: Because God only has a few people
Because every single person matters to God
Because lost people are special prizes
questions.hint: Think about how the shepherd treated the one sheep.
questions.explanation: The shepherd left to find the one because that sheep mattered to him. In the same way, every single person matters deeply to God.

questions.text: The parable shows that God gives up on people who wander away.
questions.hint: Did the shepherd give up?
questions.explanation: False! The shepherd didn't give up — he searched until he found the sheep. God never gives up on us either.

questions.text: If your friend feels far from God or left out, what could you do this week?
options: Invite them and show them they matter
Tell them to figure it out
questions.hint: Be like the caring shepherd.
questions.explanation: Like the shepherd who searched for the one, we can show others they matter by including them and pointing them to Jesus.

questions.text: What can you do when you feel like you've wandered away from God by making a bad choice?
options: Turn back to God, who is happy to welcome you
questions.hint: Heaven celebrates when you come back.
questions.explanation: When we turn back to God, all of heaven celebrates. God is always happy to welcome us home.

questions.text: How can you be part of God's kingdom according to the lesson?
options: By trusting Jesus, who made a way for you
questions.hint: Remember the Bottom Line.
questions.explanation: Jesus made a way for every single person to be part of God's kingdom by dying for us. We come in by trusting and following Him.

questions.text: The prayer this week thanks Jesus for coming to ______ us when we were lost.
questions.hint: It's what the shepherd did for the sheep.
questions.explanation: The prayer thanks Jesus for coming to find us when we were lost, just like the shepherd found his sheep.

questions.text: What is one way you can 'stay close' to the Shepherd every day?
options: Pray, read your Bible, and follow Jesus
questions.hint: The prayer asks for help to stay close, trust, and follow.
questions.explanation: We can stay close to Jesus by praying, reading the Bible, trusting Him, and following Him every day.

questions.text: Jesus is sometimes called the Good Shepherd who cares for His people.
questions.hint: Think about who searches for the lost.
questions.explanation: True! This parable shows Jesus as the caring shepherd who searches for and carries home the lost.

questions.text: Jesus made a way for you to be God's forever ______.
questions.hint: Someone close who loves you.
questions.explanation: The lesson says Jesus made a way for every person to be part of God's kingdom and be His forever friend!

questions.text: Which everyday things did Jesus use in His parables to teach about God?
questions.hint: Simple things from daily life long ago.
questions.explanation: Jesus used everyday things like seeds, coins, and sheep to help people understand big truths about God.

questions.text: How does God feel when someone who was far away comes close to Him again?
questions.hint: Same feeling as the shepherd who found his sheep.
questions.explanation: Jesus wanted everyone to know that when someone far from God comes close again, God is really, really happy.

questions.text: Why is it good news that the shepherd searched for the ONE sheep instead of saying 'at least I have 99'?
options: Because it shows God comes after each of us personally
questions.hint: Think about what it means for YOU.
questions.explanation: Most people would say 'at least he has 99,' but the shepherd went after the one. This shows God doesn't see us as a crowd — He comes after each one of us personally.

story.summary: Jesus loved telling parables — short stories that use everyday things to teach big truths about God. Everywhere He went, all kinds of people came to listen, and some grumpy religious leaders complained that Jesus spent time with people who made bad choices. So Jesus told a story: a shepherd had one hundred sheep, but one wandered off. Even though he still had ninety-nine, the shepherd cared so much that he went out searching until he found the lost one. When he found it, he wasn't angry — he was joyful! He carried it home and called out, 'Come celebrate with me! I found my sheep!' Jesus explained that all of heaven celebrates when even one person turns back to God. Every one of us is like that lost sheep; sin takes us far from God. But Jesus made a way home by dying on the cross to pay for our sins, because we matter so much to Him. Just like the shepherd carried the sheep, Jesus carries us back to God. Jesus made a way for you to be part of God's kingdom and be His forever friend!

scenes.title: Jesus Tells a Story
scenes.description: Crowds of all kinds of people gathered to hear Jesus. Some religious leaders grumbled that He spent time with people who made bad choices, but Jesus wanted everyone to know how much God cares. So He began to tell a parable about a shepherd and his sheep.

scenes.title: One Sheep Wanders Off
scenes.description: The shepherd had one hundred sheep — a big job! But sheep aren't very good at paying attention. They munch and wander until they get stuck. One sheep wandered away and became lost.

scenes.title: The Shepherd Searches
scenes.description: Most people would say, 'At least he still has ninety-nine others.' But the shepherd cared so much that he left to go searching. He didn't give up, because that one sheep mattered to him.

scenes.title: Found and Carried Home
scenes.description: The shepherd found his sheep! He wasn't angry — he was joyful. He carried it home and called out, 'Come celebrate with me!' Jesus said that all of heaven celebrates when even one person turns back to God.

scenes.title: Jesus Makes a Way Home
scenes.description: Jesus explained that every person is like that lost sheep — sin takes us far from God. But Jesus made a way home by dying on the cross because we matter so much to Him. Just like the shepherd carried the sheep, Jesus carries us into God's kingdom as His forever friends.

scenes.title: Living It Out This Week
scenes.description: Because Jesus searched for us, we can stay close to Him and help others know they matter too. We pray, read our Bibles, and follow the Good Shepherd every day — and remember our memory verse about God's kingdom.
